title: Introduce RAG step-library and sandboxed quickstart
author: Priya Nair
commits: feat: add baseline step-library README and example orchestrator
chore: add telemetry probe schema and basic probes.json
docs: document step templates and migration notes
fix: tighten types in minimal-orchestrator and update sample env vars
test: add smoke test for orchestrator startup in CI
description:
Context and motivation: This PR introduces a compact "step-library" quickstart for RAG-driven agents. The goal is to provide teams with a small, composable set of step templates (intent extraction, conditional retrieval, rerank, tool-call boundary) plus a minimal orchestrator reference that demonstrates composition patterns we recommend for production: explicit step inputs/outputs, deterministic fallbacks, and light telemetry probes. This is targeted at engineering teams who want an offline-first sandbox to iterate on prompt step composition without adopting the full agent SDK upfront.

What this change contains (single continuous description): Added a new quickstart directory (quickstarts/rag-step-library) containing: a README with guided walkthroughs and recommended invariants; three YAML step templates (intent-extract, retrieve-then-rerank, tool-call-guard) that show parameterized prompt placeholders and contract examples; a minimal TypeScript orchestrator (examples/minimal-orchestrator.ts) that wires steps together, shows how to call Redwood API endpoints for embeddings + generation, and demonstrates safe tool-call stubs for local testing; a tiny browser stub example to validate authoring without server dependencies; telemetry probes (telemetry/probes.json) which include token-level latency probes, step success/failure counters, and a synthetic prompt variance probe for guarding regressions; docs updates (docs/rag/step-library-guide.md) explaining migration from older playbook formats and the recommended rollout strategy; and a small site sidebar tweak to expose the quickstart on docs site. All templates are intentionally minimal and annotated with authoring tips (prompt variant hooks, expected KV-cache behavior).

Checklist / testing performed: - Local smoke run of minimal-orchestrator with mock tool adapter (passed) - CI: added smoke test that starts orchestrator and runs three end-to-end steps against local mocks (flaky first run; reran and passed) - Linting/formatting: Prettier/ESLint clean - Docs spellchecked and cross-linked to existing RAG authoring pages - Telemetry: probes.json validated against the probes schema used by the Console ingestion shim

Backward compatibility and migration notes: No breaking surface changes to Redwood APIs. The quickstart uses the public REST + SDK access patterns; customers can adopt templates incrementally. Migration guidance included in docs/rag/step-library-guide.md outlines mapping from legacy stateless playbook YAML to these step templates (including recommended schema for inputs, outputs, and error handling).

Security and privacy: Example orchestrator defaults to non-production keys and includes a clear warning block in the README about secrets handling. The browser stub is intentionally client-only and does not persist any index data.

Review conversation summary: Carlos: "Love the step contracts—can we add an explicit schema example for error objects so consumers have consistent retry logic?" — Priya: "Added error-object example to intent-extract.yaml and expanded migration doc paragraph describing retry semantics." Ava: "Telemetry probes look good; can we ensure probes.json uses the same probe IDs used in Console?" — Priya: "Validated probe IDs against Console ingestion shim; updated probes.json and added comment." Samir: "CI flake observed on first smoke run, but rerun passed; add retry to that job." — Priya: "Added a single-retry wrapper for the smoke job in the workflow (non-blocking)." Approvals: Carlos (approved), Ava (approved), Samir (approved after second LGTM).

CI status: initial run showed one flaky smoke test; rerun succeeded. All status checks green at merge time.

Release notes: Adds a new Quickstart: "RAG step-library and sandboxed orchestrator" — intended for docs site and quickstart gallery; no API changes.

Related work / references: Linear ENG-2148 (step contract formalization), PM-8790 (quickstart UX placement). Linked support ticket SUP-553 reported a gap in small, composable authoring examples which motivated the quickstart.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main. Follow-up: open an RFC to standardize step error contract (ENG-2202) and add a TypeScript SDK helper for step wiring (planned as a small subsequent PR).
